rows.description: The student concludes that one failure means a ruined future and stops studying. The thought feels certain but skips the evidence, and it makes real recovery less likely.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, cutting losses, lateral thinking, learning from past failure, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: telling parents and asking for support [Action]
rows.description: Afraid of anger, the student still shares the result and a draft recovery plan with parents, who after the initial upset help arrange a supplementary attempt and extra doubt sessions.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, cutting losses, lateral thinking, learning from past failure, seeking advice
related mind states: anger, fear, doubt

rows.description: The student conceals the marksheet and hopes to fix things quietly. The secrecy adds fear, delays practical steps such as re-exam applications and damages trust when the truth emerges.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: cutting losses, lateral thinking, learning from past failure, seeking advice
related mind states: fear, hope, trust

rows.description: The student learns about supplementary exams, open school and other pathways, and sees that one result is a setback within a longer route rather than the end of options.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, cutting losses, lateral thinking, learning from past failure, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: rebuilding with a smaller first target [Action]
rows.description: Rather than an immediate topper plan, the student aims to clear the weakest subject first with a weekly plan and a mentor, using the early success to restart momentum.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, cutting losses, lateral thinking, learning from past failure

rows.subtype: Approach: learning from past failure as data [Thinking]
rows.description: The student compares this exam with an earlier success, noting sleep, revision method and stress differences, and treats the failure as information about what to change.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, cutting losses, lateral thinking, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: asking for professional help when hopeless [Revision]
rows.description: If sadness and hopelessness persist, the student and parents approach the school counsellor or a helpline, since heavy despair after failure needs care from trained people and not only willpower.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, cutting losses, lateral thinking, learning from past failure, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: revising the meaning of the result [Revision]
rows.description: After some weeks and talking to older cousins who also struggled, the student reframes the result as one stage, keeps a smaller goal, and is more ready to seek help earlier next time.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, cutting losses, learning from past failure, seeking advice

rows.description: Before joining a student march about fee hikes, the teen reads the notice, the college statement and reports from different outlets, checking who organises it and what exactly is being demanded.

rows.subtopic: Deciding whether to join a protest
rows.description: The teen asks which principle matters most, such as fairness or safety, and whether joining serves that cause, or whether a letter, petition or school council meeting might achieve it better.
